prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1156; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant's account changed in important ways between conversations: the direction of the impact and the number of people in the car are now different.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a report of a low-speed collision in a shopping center parking lot. The insured driver is named on the policy, and the claimant reported being the driver of the second vehicle involved.
Entry 2: Initial statement taken from the claimant by phone. The claimant reports a wrist injury from the impact and says the other vehicle backed into the claimant's car while it was parked.
Entry 3: Police report obtained. It confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the incident and lists the other driver's account, which matches the reported sequence of events.
Entry 4: Photos from the scene and the other driver's statement are on file. Two independent witnesses in the lot describe the collision as it was reported to us.
Entry 5: Vehicle inspected. Most of the damage is consistent with the described impact, and no prior damage to the vehicle is recorded in our files or in the appraiser's notes. Nothing suggests the damage predates the coverage start.
Entry 6: Medical records received. The wrist fracture is consistent with the kind and force of the crash, and no earlier injury to the same area appears in the claimant's history. Treatment followed a typical course and eased as the claimant improved.
Entry 7: Follow-up call with the claimant. The account has changed in important ways since the first conversation: the claimant now describes the impact coming from a different direction and recalls a different number of people in the car. The claimant was asked to clarify both points in writing.
Entry 8: Claim file reviewed against the police report, witness statements, photos, inspection notes, and medical records. The core facts are supported, but the claimant's revised account on impact direction and occupants still needs to be addressed before settlement discussions proceed.
